name: GET /api/dev/otp
note: Cell question: can this actor obtain a LIVE sign-in code for an account that already exists? Deny x12. The endpoint itself carries no authentication at all — it is a dev helper, gated only on NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV in (development, preview) at route.ts:5-8 — so "every actor reaches it" is by design and is not the cell. The gate that IS the cell is route.ts:34-44: any phone with a profiles row is answered 404 {"error":"not found"} and the pending code is withheld (the R1 hardening, spec §4.4 decision #6). Probed against a phone that has BOTH a profiles row and a fresh dev_otp_inbox row, so a 404 proves withholding rather than absence; the no-profile control (a code IS served) is asserted by name. Three properties this verdict cannot carry — the response-body oracle, the timing oracle that survives fixing it, and the unauthenticated service-role DELETE at lines 17-20 — are recorded in docs/security/row-scope-app.json instead.

name: audit_log_immutable
note: Returns trigger. Live proacl is `=X/postgres | postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`: the leading =X/postgres is the PUBLIC default, and anon and authenticated each hold an EXPLICIT EXECUTE on top of it, so a revoke aimed at PUBLIC alone would not remove either. On paper anon may call it -- but PostgREST excludes trigger-returning functions from its schema cache (PGRST202 on both POST and GET /rpc), and the PL/pgSQL call handler refuses one in any non-trigger context regardless of role: `select public.set_updated_at()` run as the postgres superuser fails with 'trigger functions can only be called as triggers'. Deny x12. The cell itself cannot resolve past needs-live-proof because PGRST202 is never proof of a privilege decision (verdict.ts); the question is settled by name instead -- assertion function:<name>.no-rpc-route.
